source: Spotify official: support.spotify.com (US articles), www.spotify.com/us/premium/, newsroom.spotify.com
verification_method: Independent re-fetch of each of the 42 unique URLs once (python urllib via configured proxy, one browser UA, 3.5 s between fetches, all HTTP 200 on 2026-10-04). Quotes checked as exact substrings of text extracted from the raw HTML (scripts/styles removed, inline tags joined without spaces, block tags as spaces, entities unescaped, whitespace collapsed); 92/93 found in visible text, 1 (#89) found verbatim only in the page's raw __NEXT_DATA__ keyword metadata, as that finding itself states. Dates checked against updatedAt (support) / datePublished (newsroom): all match. Each claim read against the quote and the surrounding article text.

findings.claim: Spotify Local Files plays audio files already stored on the device; the official article describes no upload or cloud storage of those files.
findings.quote: Along with the millions of tracks Spotify offers, you can also use the app to play any of the audio files legally stored on your device.

findings.claim: On iOS and Android, Local Files is turned on per device with a "Local audio files" switch under Settings and privacy > Apps and devices.
findings.quote: Tap Apps and devices. Switch Local audio files on

findings.claim: On iOS the files must be copied into a Spotify folder under "On My iPhone" (via the Files app, Universal Clipboard over iCloud, or USB from Finder/iTunes), i.e. each phone needs its own copy of the files.
findings.quote: Tap Browse and go to the folder On My iPhone. Tap and press the folder for Spotify. Select Paste or Move Item here. Your stored music is now in Local Files.

findings.claim: On iOS, the Spotify folder can disappear from On My iPhone if its Help file is deleted (known limitation, fixed by restarting the app).
findings.quote: The Spotify folder may disappear from On My iPhone if the Help file within it is deleted. To display the folder again, restart the Spotify app.

findings.claim: On Android, files must first be downloaded or transferred (e.g. USB / file-transfer app) onto the device itself.
findings.quote: Open the app that can browse and manage the file, such as Google’s Drive app. Find the option to Download the file (ex. More > Download)

findings.claim: On desktop, Local Files is enabled in Settings > Library ("Show Local Files") and reads from folders the user selects or adds as a source.
findings.quote: Scroll to Library and switch Show Local Files on . Under Show songs from, turn on the folders you want Local Files to have access to. Or, click Add a source to select another folder.

findings.claim: Crossfade between local files only works when the files share the same sample rate and channel count.
findings.quote: When crossfade is enabled, Spotify will crossfade between local files that use the same sample rate and channel count (mono/stereo).

findings.claim: Official troubleshooting for Local Files is to remove local files from playlists and start over, or do a clean reinstall (which also wipes downloads).
findings.quote: Remove local files from any playlists you might have added them to, then start over the steps for adding Local Files

findings.claim: Downloading music (albums, playlists) requires Premium; Free users can only download podcasts.
findings.quote: On Premium, you can download albums, playlists, and podcasts. On the free version, you can only download podcasts.

findings.claim: Download limit per the Listen offline article: up to 10,000 tracks on each of up to 5 devices.
findings.quote: You can download as many as 10,000 tracks on each of up to 5 different devices.

findings.claim: The Premium benefits article words the same limit differently: a maximum of 10,000 tracks across up to 5 devices (the two official articles are inconsistent).
findings.quote: A maximum of 10,000 tracks can be downloaded across up to 5 devices.

findings.claim: Users must go online at least once every 30 days to keep downloads.
findings.quote: You need to go online at least once every 30 days to keep your downloads. This is so Spotify can collect play data to compensate artists.

findings.claim: Individual songs cannot be downloaded on their own; they must be put in a playlist first.
findings.quote: Note: You can’t download individual songs, but you can put them in a playlist and download the playlist.

findings.claim: Downloading to a 6th device removes downloads from the least recently used device; reinstalling the app also loses downloads.
findings.quote: You download to more than 5 devices Note: Downloads are removed from the device you’ve used least recently.

findings.claim: Downloads use Wi-Fi by default; cellular downloading is an opt-in setting.
findings.quote: Spotify uses WiFi to download by default to save mobile data usage, but you can allow downloading on mobile data:

findings.claim: Offline Mode makes only downloaded content playable and greys out everything else.
findings.quote: Anything you haven’t downloaded is now grayed out and unavailable.

findings.claim: Offline Backup (Premium, phones, Android Auto, CarPlay) auto-builds an offline playlist from cached recent listens, with no manual downloads.
findings.quote: For: Premium on mobile phones, Android Auto, and CarPlay Offline Backup is filled with music you can play offline. No downloads required.

findings.claim: Background downloads on iOS (downloads continue while the app is closed, with progress notifications) rolled out to Premium in May 2026.
findings.quote: We’ve made offline listening more dependable with the rollout of background downloads on iOS. Your music and podcasts will keep downloading even when the app isn’t open, and you’ll see notifications showing their progress.

findings.claim: Since Feb 2026, lyrics are saved automatically with downloaded tracks (Premium).
findings.quote: Now, when you download your favorite tracks for offline listening, the lyrics will automatically be saved too.

findings.claim: On mobile and tablet, the Play Queue is labelled as a Premium feature (desktop/web section carries no such label).
findings.quote: Mobile and tablet For: Premium Open the queue

findings.claim: Queue supports add, drag-to-reorder, swipe-to-remove and Clear queue.
findings.quote: In the Play Queue, tap and hold next to the track. Drag and drop it to the position you want.

findings.claim: In May 2025 Premium got a redesigned queue with Shuffle, Smart Shuffle, Repeat and Sleep Timer controls, plus a preview of autoplay recommendations after the queue ends.
findings.quote: The new design is easier to use and includes controls like Shuffle, Smart Shuffle, Repeat, and Sleep Timer.

findings.claim: In May 2026 Premium regained multi-select in the play queue, and all users got in-playlist bulk actions.
findings.quote: And for Premium users, we’ve brought back the ability to select and manage multiple songs in your play queue at once.

findings.claim: Premium users can choose between two shuffle styles: "Fewer repeats" and "Standard".
findings.quote: Choosing shuffle play styles For: Premium You can choose between two shuffle styles:

findings.claim: Since Nov 2025 the default shuffle is "Fewer Repeats" (accounts for recent listening); Premium can switch back to Standard, and Free and Premium can tap a song while shuffling to play it next without reshuffling.
findings.quote: We’ve also updated our default Shuffle so you’ll get Fewer Repeats when you listen.

findings.claim: Smart Shuffle (mixes in recommendations) is always on for Free mobile users; Premium can turn it on per playlist or switch it out of the play modes.
findings.quote: For listeners on free (mobile) Smart Shuffle is always active on mobile.

findings.claim: A one-tap reshuffle button for Premium on mobile launched in May 2026.
findings.quote: Mix up the order of your shuffle anytime with the reshuffle button.

findings.claim: Repeat cycles album/playlist repeat and single-song repeat (press twice).
findings.quote: Repeat album, playlist, or song When it ends, it starts again! Select twice to repeat a song.

findings.claim: Crossfade is a Premium feature with an adjustable length; Automix (beat-matched, select playlists) is also Premium; gapless playback has no Premium label.
findings.quote: Crossfade For: Premium Overlaps 2 tracks by fading out of the first while fading in the next.

findings.claim: Crossfade, Automix and gapless cannot be set while using Spotify Connect.
findings.quote: Note: You can’t set these features when using Spotify Connect.

findings.claim: Mixed Playlists (Premium) add custom per-transition volume, EQ and effects with BPM/key shown per song; Free users hear them as normal playlists.
findings.quote: On Premium, you can listen to the playlist with transitions. On the free version, you can only listen to it as a regular playlist.

findings.claim: Smart Reorder (Feb 2026) re-sequences a mixed playlist by BPM and key in one tap for Premium.
findings.quote: With one tap, this upgrade gives Premium users an easy way to rearrange mixed playlists with BPM and key.

findings.claim: Sleep Timer is one of the controls in the redesigned Premium queue (Sept 2025 recap of the May 2025 change). No dedicated support article on the sleep timer appears in the support site navigation.
findings.quote: Premium users can enjoy a redesigned queue with upgraded controls that make it easier to shuffle, Smart Shuffle, repeat, or add a Sleep Timer.

findings.claim: Playback speed is documented only for podcasts (with 15-second skip/rewind); no music playback-speed control was found in the support or newsroom pages checked.
findings.quote: Tap to control the play speed. Tap to skip forward 15 seconds, or to rewind 15 seconds.

findings.claim: Playlist folders can be created on desktop, web player and mobile and show on all devices; nested folders are supported.
findings.quote: You need to use the desktop app, web player, and mobile app to make playlist folders, but they show on all devices.

findings.claim: Folders can contain folders.

findings.claim: Any playlist can be made collaborative so friends can add, remove and reorder tracks.

findings.claim: Songs, albums, artists, playlists, podcasts and profiles can be shared by link, to social/messaging apps, or as a scannable Spotify Code; desktop also offers embed code.

findings.claim: Music quality is not adjustable on the web player.

findings.claim: Lossless must be enabled manually on each device.

findings.claim: Recon claim "Local Files does not upload to the cloud; files must be on each device": CONFIRMED (implied, not stated in those words: the official article only describes playing files stored on the device and gives separate copy-to-device steps for iOS, Android and desktop; it never mentions uploading, cloud storage or syncing local files between devices.)
findings.quote: Along with the millions of tracks Spotify offers, you can also use the app to play any of the audio files legally stored on your device.

findings.claim: Recon claim "Local Files supports mp3, m4p, mp4": NOT FOUND (The current official Local Files article (updated 2025-06-30) lists no supported file formats at all. "MP3" and "M4P" appear only in the page's hidden search-keyword metadata (raw JSON), which is not a statement of format support; "mp4" does not appear. The recon claim comes from a third-party site (soundguys.com), not from Spotify.)
